name: Covert Exfiltration Rule 0083

metadata:
  uuid: 0982e504-d1b0-4624-87de-5d03192f85d7
  schema: rule::1.0
  version: 8
  created: 2025-03-31
  modified: 2025-06-03
  tlp: amber+strict
  author: Corpus Generator
  contributors:
    - Detection Engineering
  organisation:
    uuid: 00f75f5a-ad4d-457a-8c78-308fdf11b679
    name: Example Detection Team

description: |
  Generated detection rule 83.
  It looks for powershell.exe launched in an unusual way.
status: IMPROVING
severity: Medium
techniques:
  - T1003.001
  - T1218
  - T1490
detection_model: 70ebd555-56ab-48c4-b147-2d3e67236e1e

response:
  alert_severity: Medium
  responders: SOC Tier 2
  procedure:
    analysis: |
      Review the process tree and the account that ran it.
    searches:
      - purpose: Other executions on the host
        system: sentinel
        query: |
          DeviceProcessEvents
          | where FileName =~ "psexec.exe"
      - purpose: Logons of the account
        system: splunk
        query: |
          index=main sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624
    containment: Isolate the host if the activity is confirmed.

configurations:
  defender_for_endpoint:
    enabled: true
    name: Covert Exfiltration Rule 0083
    status: STAGING
    query: |
      DeviceNetworkEvents
      | where RemotePort == 4444
      | project Timestamp, DeviceId, ReportId, RemoteIP, RemotePort
    scheduling: "1H"
    alert:
      category: Execution
      severity: Medium
    impacted_entities:
      device: DeviceId
    scope:
      selection: All
  elastic:
    enabled: true
    name: Covert Exfiltration Rule 0083
    schema: platform::elastic::1.0
    status: DEVELOPMENT
    type: query
    language: kuery
    query: |
      process.pid: abc
    index:
      - logs-endpoint.events.*
    scheduling:
      interval: "10m"
      lookback: "1m"
    severity:
      default: high
      mapping:
        - field: host.os.type
          value: windows
          operator: equals
          severity: high
